literal: Like the gods even if they live, greatness they are without indeed, wife's bamboo resembling shoulders those who fear.
translation: Even if they live a life like that of the gods, men who fear their wife's bamboo-like shoulders have no true greatness.
modern: தம் மனைவியின் மூங்கில் போன்ற தோள்களைக் கண்டு அஞ்சுகின்ற கணவர்கள், தேவர்களைப் போலச் சிறந்த வாழ்க்கை வாழ்ந்தாலும் எந்தப் பெருமையும் இல்லாதவர்களே ஆவர்.
explanation: This couplet criticizes men who are overly submissive to their wives out of fear. The phrase 'அமையார்தோள்' (bamboo-like shoulders) is a classical metaphor for a woman's beautiful, smooth shoulders, highlighting the irony of fearing something so delicate. 'இமையார்' refers to the gods, who are traditionally believed not to blink. The poet states that even if such men achieve a heavenly, god-like status in life, their cowardly submission strips them of all true dignity and greatness ('பாடு').
